headline: Taste Over Credentials: A Different Kind of AI Job
lede: Most prompt engineering listings read like conventional tech postings — degrees, years of experience, familiarity with model architectures. A job posting from @nickfloats ignores all of that. The requirements are two: good taste, and an obsession with the tools.
body:
The contrast with the mainstream market is sharp. Platforms like Turing and Indeed list dozens of prompt engineering roles, most draped in familiar tech-industry language — CS degrees, two-plus years of relevant experience, deliverables tied to marketing funnels or enterprise chatbots. Anthropic itself posted a "Prompt Engineer and Librarian" position at up to $335,000, signaling that the job title had arrived in corporate legitimacy. What @nickfloats is advertising sits in a different tradition entirely.

The scope is deliberately wide: image, video, music, and **language models** all in play. This sweep across the *generative AI* stack — visual, sonic, textual — reflects how creative work with these systems has evolved. The most interesting outputs increasingly require navigating several modalities in sequence, setting a visual mood in one tool, a sonic texture in another, then binding them together through precise language. No single specialization is sufficient.

The phrase "artist led research" carries real weight. It locates the role not in the benchmark-and-evaluation culture of AI labs but in a tradition closer to practice-based inquiry — the kind associated with design studios, experimental residencies, and art-school research programs. The researcher's primary instrument is the model itself; the output is knowledge about what these systems can and cannot do when pressed by someone with genuine aesthetic commitments, not just technical fluency.

There is a growing argument in AI circles that *taste* — the capacity to distinguish a remarkable output from a merely plausible one — is the decisive skill that separates useful prompting from mechanical prompting. If that argument holds, hiring for it directly is more honest than inferring it from a resume. The informal channel (reply or DM) reinforces the point: this is a role being filled through a community of practitioners, not an applicant tracking system.

concepts.definition: AI systems trained to produce new content — images, audio, video, text — rather than merely classify or analyze existing content. They are prompted with natural-language or other inputs and return novel outputs based on patterns learned from large datasets.

AI systems that work across more than one type of content, such as text, image, audio, or video. A multimodal workflow might use a language model to write a script, an image model to generate visuals, and a music model to score it — often in combination.

A mode of inquiry in which creative practice is the primary research method, rather than controlled experiments or hypothesis testing. Common in design schools and art-technology labs, it produces knowledge about what tools can do through the act of making with them.

The craft of writing precise instructions — prompts — that guide AI models toward desired outputs. Sometimes called context engineering, it ranges from simple phrasing choices to complex multi-step instruction sequences and has become a recognized professional specialty.
